answer: Each Ember Cartographer node keeps a cryptographic mirror of its identity ledger and signs a daily nonce that updates a reputation score, which rises with continuous task completion and fades when the node is idle. To launch a Sybil attack, an adversary must create a fake identity, then perform a sonnet‑scale series of genuine tasks—each consuming computational work roughly equal to a juniper’s yearly growth—so the counterfeit node can accrue enough reputation to be accepted, making the cost grow linearly with each additional fake node.
